plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives in cool fall weather and is a staple of autumn gardens across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia, especially China and Japan
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,000 years, and the flower is the national symbol of Japan, where the Chrysanthemum Throne is named for it.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous tree whose canopy is covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. It blooms in the Southern Hemisphere spring and carpets streets with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Grafton, Sydney), and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, there are about 70,000 jacaranda trees, and there is a local saying that a bloom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces crocus-like pink-lilac flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The foliage emerges the following spring and dies back by summer.
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe, from the UK to the Balkans; grown in gardens in temperate regions
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid. It is used in medicine for gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A daisy-like annual with feathery foliage and tall, airy stems topped with saucer-shaped flowers. It keeps blooming until the first frost and attracts butterflies and bees in late season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to first frost (June to late October in temperate zones)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and the southwestern US; cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony, a name given by Spanish priests who grew the plants in their mission gardens in Mexico.
